newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo to stand trial Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo to stand trial Dec 11.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, who has singled out high-ranking government officials in his crusade against corruption, will stand trial December 11 for calling a High Court judge "a corrupt thief."
The Argentine news agency DyN reported Friday that Federal Judge Adolfo Bagnasco set the date for the trial after Cavallo's retractions were twice rejected.

The case dates back to 1993, when Cavallo called two Supreme Court judges, Augusto Belluscio and Enrique Petracchi, "corrupt thieves" for their ruling in a case against the central bank. Both filed suit, but Petracchi accepted a retraction last month.
Belluscio said it was "too late" for Cavallo after two attempts at retraction, which the judge said he considered "light" excuses rather than apologies.
"He did not take back what he said or admit he gravely offended my honor," said the judge.
Cavallo, praised for bringing hyperinflation under control and fostering growth during his tenure as economy minister, was sacked in July.
He later whipped up a political storm by accusing two ministers and President Carlos Menem's top aide of covering up corruption. They deny the allegations and at least one plans to sue him.
